guide: Open Start here and type your agency name, your cash floor, the planned owner draw and your targets in the yellow cells: profit share, overhead share, cash cover weeks and the 1,000-hour marker (a marker, not a rule).
Check Team, Expenses and Budget. Overhead by month, the budget actual and the profit and loss overhead read the Expenses sheet, so every payment is typed once.

Type each month on Profit and Loss: revenue, billed hours and caregiver pay lines. Margin, profit, shares and break-even hours fill in. Payroll burden means payroll taxes, insurance and benefits on top of pay (confirm with your adviser).

Keep Cash Months, Pay Runs and Expected Receipts up to date. The 13-Week Cash Forecast shows Base, Best and Worst, the lowest week and what happens if third-party payers (an insurer or a public body) pay later.
Use Owner Draws and Tax Set-Aside each month. The Safe Owner Draw tool gives the largest draw that keeps cash above the floor. Every tax and pay amount is an example: confirm with your adviser.
Read Health Score History and Health Targets. Each of six measures is scored from the target to the red limit; the worst item shows what to fix first. Edit the targets to your own.
Use the Hours Target Plan, Break-Even Scenarios and the scenario tools before a rate rise, a decision about a weak client or a hire. Gross margin per hour means bill rate minus loaded pay cost.
A one-person agency can start with Enquiries, Quotes, Schedule (a rota or roster), Visits, Payroll, Invoices and Cash; Start-up Pages and the Start-up Mode tool show what to hide until you grow.
Use the 18 decision tools: each ends with a verdict and a what-if table. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready messages.
Replace the demo data with your own: clear the demo rows, type your own months and keep the dates as real dates. The workbook has no macros and works in Excel and Google Sheets.

Why a workbook: one flat price, no per-client or per-caregiver fee, your data stays with you, and reports built for agency owners. It takes typed or pasted figures: no live app, no GPS and no automatic check-in.

listing.title: Home Care Agency Owner Dashboard Excel Template: Profit and Loss, 13-Week Cash Forecast, Safe Owner Draw, Break-Even Hours, Health Score
listing.headline: Know if your home care agency is healthy: profit, cash, hours and draw
listing.description:
Run the money side of a small home care agency in one Excel workbook. Built for an owner-director with a scheduler, an office manager and a part-time recruiter, and for a one-person start-up agency that wants to begin with the pages it needs.

Profit and Loss turns revenue from billed hours, caregiver pay, overtime, travel, payroll burden and overhead into gross margin, profit and every share. Expenses feed Overhead by Month and the Budget, so each payment is typed once. Cash Months, Pay Runs and Expected Receipts feed a 13-Week Cash Forecast in Base, Best and Worst, with a floor warning, weeks of cover and a payer-pays-later slider.

18 decision tools answer the questions an owner asks every week, each with a verdict: Is the agency healthy? (one score from six measures with the worst item first), safe owner draw, tax set-aside (confirm with your adviser), lowest cash week and credit needed, hours target planner with the 1,000-hour marker, break-even weekly hours, rate rise, weakest client and scheduler scenarios, budget against actual and start-up mode. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists, send 34 ready messages and read 30 live figures and 22 charts on the owner dashboard.

This is part eight of the Home Care Agency Business suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, one flat price with no per-client or per-caregiver fee, your data stays with you, 15 languages in one purchase, with a demo copy full of sample data. Tax, pay and insurance figures are examples: confirm with your adviser and check your own local rules. The workbook holds money, hours and dates only and does not promise results.

The tax set-aside is planned at {set:tax_set_aside_pct} of profit. This is a sample rate: confirm the rate, the amounts and the dates with your adviser and check your own local rules.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own agency; check your own local rules and confirm tax, pay and insurance matters with your adviser.

documents.title: Year-end pack for the accountant
paragraphs: Year-end pack of {set:company} to {col:pnl.month}, dated {today}.
Revenue this year to date {col:pnl.ytd_revenue}. Profit this year to date {col:pnl.ytd_profit}. Caregiver pay in the last 12 months {col:pnl.annual_pay}.

Attach: the profit and loss by month, the expenses list, the pay run totals, the owner draws, the tax set-aside record and the client invoice and payment totals. Ask your accountant which other papers are needed; check your own local rules.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own agency; check your own local rules and confirm tax, pay and insurance matters with your adviser.

documents.title: Break-even report for one month
paragraphs: Break-even report of {set:company} for {col:pnl.month}, dated {today}.
Gross margin per billed hour {col:pnl.margin_hour}. Overhead {col:pnl.overhead}. Break-even weekly hours {col:pnl.breakeven_hours} against weekly hours of {col:pnl.weekly_hours}.
Weekly hours are growing by {col:pnl.hours_growth} a month, so the {set:office_help_hours}-hour marker for office help is about {col:pnl.months_to_marker} months away (99 means no growth).
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own agency; check your own local rules and confirm tax, pay and insurance matters with your adviser.

documents.title: Hours target plan report
paragraphs: Hours target plan of {set:company}, dated {today}. Plan: {col:hplan.plan}.
Weekly hours in the plan {col:hplan.weekly_hours} at a margin of {col:hplan.margin_hour} per hour. Overhead {col:hplan.overhead} a month and an owner draw of {col:hplan.draw} a month.

Profit after the draw {col:hplan.profit_after_draw}. Weekly hours needed {col:hplan.needed_hours}, gap {col:hplan.hours_gap} (plus is short). Caregivers to add {col:hplan.caregivers_needed} by {col:hplan.hire_by}.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own agency; check your own local rules and confirm tax, pay and insurance matters with your adviser.

documents.title: Health score report with six measures
paragraphs: Health score report of {set:company} for {col:health.month}, dated {today}.

Gross margin per hour {col:health.margin_hour} ({col:health.p_margin} points). Overtime share {col:health.overtime_share} ({col:health.p_overtime}). Fill rate {col:health.fill_rate} ({col:health.p_fill}). Days to be paid {col:health.days_to_pay} ({col:health.p_days}).
Caregiver turnover {col:health.turnover_rate} ({col:health.p_turnover}). Weeks of cash cover {col:health.cover_weeks} ({col:health.p_cover}).
Health score {col:health.score} out of 100. Worst item: {col:health.worst}. Targets are examples: replace them with your own.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own agency; check your own local rules and confirm tax, pay and insurance matters with your adviser.

documents.title: Scenario comparison for one scenario
paragraphs: Scenario of {set:company}, dated {today}: {col:breakeven.scenario}.
Rate rise {col:breakeven.rate_rise}, hours lost {col:breakeven.hours_lost}, office help {col:breakeven.scheduler_cost} a month. Margin per hour after {col:breakeven.new_margin}.
Weekly hours after {col:breakeven.hours_after} against break-even at {col:breakeven.breakeven_hours}. Profit a month {col:breakeven.profit_month}: {col:breakeven.verdict}.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own agency; check your own local rules and confirm tax, pay and insurance matters with your adviser.

documents.title: Overhead report by line
paragraphs: Overhead report of {set:company} for {col:overhead.month}, dated {today}.

Rent {col:overhead.rent}, office payroll {col:overhead.office_payroll}, field supervisor pay {col:overhead.field_pay}, software and phones {col:overhead.software_phones}, insurance {col:overhead.insurance}, marketing and recruiting {col:overhead.marketing_recruiting}, other {col:overhead.other}.
Total overhead {col:overhead.total}, which is {col:overhead.share_of_revenue} of revenue against a target of {set:overhead_share_target}.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own agency; check your own local rules and confirm tax, pay and insurance matters with your adviser.

documents.title: One-person start-up plan for one page
paragraphs: Start-up plan of {set:company}, dated {today}. Page: {col:startup.page} ({col:startup.part}).
Used by a one-person agency: {col:startup.one_person}. Switch it on from {col:startup.from_caregivers} caregivers. {col:startup.note}.

A one-person agency can start with Enquiries, Quotes, Schedule, Visits, Payroll, Invoices and Cash and hide the rest until the agency grows. Use the Start-up Mode tool to see the next page to switch on.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own agency; check your own local rules and confirm tax, pay and insurance matters with your adviser.
